title: Stop Throwing Away Time-on-Task Data
intro: Small-sample timing data is skewed: everyone has a minimum time, but delays are open-ended.

learn.title: Eight participants, one task
learn.text:
42s · 48s · 52s · 55s · 57s · 64s · 69s · **240s** (reread, misclicked, backtracked)

**Median 56s** describes the typical experience. **Mean 78s** is pulled up by one participant.

Both are correct — they answer different questions.

try.q: Why is the median the better headline here?
options: It has a smaller margin of error
try.explain: Timing data is skewed, so the mean follows the slow tail.

learn.title: Never delete the outlier
learn.text:
Practitioners do one of two things with eight timings: dismiss them as meaningless, or **trim the slowest one** to make the report look clean.

Calabro calls trimming risky and unethical. **The slow case is usually the most important finding** — it's the failure path.

try.q: What does the 240-second participant usually represent?
options: A participant who misunderstood the task
try.explain: Deleting it removes the most important finding.

left.label: What people do
items: Trim the slowest to look clean

right.label: What to do
items: Keep and explain the slow case

learn.title: How to report it
learn.text:
**Use the median** — it represents typical observed behaviour when data is skewed.

**Show the range and the individual times** — with eight people, the individual times are often the clearest chart.

**Explain the slow cases from what you observed** — “reread the label, misclicked, backtracked” is the finding, not the number.

try.q: With eight participants, what is often the clearest chart?
try.explain: Eight dots show the shape and the outlier at once.

options: There's a floor but no ceiling
test.explain: Everyone has a minimum time; delays are open-ended.

test.q: What does the mean answer that the median doesn't?
test.explain: Both are correct; they answer different questions.

test.q: What does Calabro call trimming the slowest result?
What should accompany a slow time in the report?
options: An apology for the sample size
A comparison with the industry average
test.explain: “Reread, misclicked, backtracked” is the actual finding.

test.q: What is the common mistake besides trimming?
options: Using a stopwatch instead of software
test.explain: Eight timings tell you a lot if you report them honestly.
